chart.title: Moore's law: The number of transistors per microprocessor
chart.subtitle: Moore's law is the observation that the number of transistors in an integrated circuit doubles about every two years, thanks to improvements in production. It was first described by Gordon E. Moore, the co-founder of Intel, in 1965.
